big_picture:
Unit 9's checks are sound: every task reruns with other values, the predicts use code students can see, and the pass lines carry the story. All four reps found the same three weak spots, and I'm accepting nearly every fix for them.
(1) The ladder drops students in a few places, and the worst is bars-one-more-time. It is one blank `pass` with five pieces to build, no "what does each number mean?" step, and a last hint that stops halfway. It becomes a predict on runnable fuel_bar code and three checkpoints: blocks, then label and numbers, then the edges. Every Show-me hint is the full lines.
(2) Several steps can be passed by copying the screen just before them. The SOLO 8A fix is in warm-up Q2. SOLO 8B is mend-the-copy again, and quiz Q8 repeats it. In the Quick Check, C3 is the 8A-07 solution with one word swapped, which tests a student out of the whole unit. Each one now asks for a different decision: warm-up Q2 becomes a plain-number precedence item, SOLO 8B is a two-step function where students must find the line that drops the copy, quiz Q8 is a missing `return`, and QC C3 has a new shape and new names.
(3) Messages students can't read. The site explainer gets plain-word entries for Unit 9's slips. Every function check gets the Units 3/7 `_why` helper so an example's name (`said`) or a typo (`curent`) is explained. The unclear check messages get plain wording. u09b says "place", like u09a.
Two things stay as they are: the precedence bug in SOLO 8A (the spec's seat A, and an honest check of 8A-07's "work it out first"), and the "Mar'tu remembers" def/return rule. Q1 becomes a def/return item with a stamp and `str()`, so Unit 9 opens on the campaign's mana-bar build, not Unit 7's hardest shape.
The Quick Check becomes an honest test-out. Form A's names are renamed. A fifth question tests `.find()` -1, the class's right-shape slip, and 4 of the 5 questions are needed. C3 gets a second checkpoint where the student writes an f-string. The pass line keeps to core story beats and no longer gives away the optional project.
Optional extras for the stretch group cost no core time: a write-from-blank challenge as in Units 3 to 7, a find-the-comma bonus, and "why" angles. Core time goes from about 60 to about 62 minutes (8A is 20 to 22 for the bar predict and split).

site_requests: src/lib/course/explain.ts: add plain-word entries for Unit 9's slips. Each one uses the student's own names from the failing line, has a lean-mode kind name (for SOLO and Quick Check items), and gets explain.test.ts cases. (1) "TypeError: 'str' object does not support item assignment" (8A-03's planned first crash, 8A-01, Quiz 8A): "Text can't change one letter. Build a new one and put it back: `word = \"G\" + word[1:]`." Take the variable and letter from the line. Lean kind: 'text changed in place'. (2) "AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'join'" (8B-03, 8B-09, Quiz 8B, 8P1): "A list can't join itself. Ask the glue: `\" \".join(words)`." Use the line's own glue and list. (3) "AttributeError: 'builtin_function_or_method' object has no attribute 'X'" (8B-09 CP1, a chain missing its middle `()`): "`note` holds an order, not text: the line above wrote `.lower` with no `()`. Python runs a method only with `()`." Point at the assigning line when there is one (`note = note.lower`), else at the same line's chain (`raw.lower.capitalize()`). (4) "AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'lower'|'upper'|'strip'|'replace'|'find'|'split'" (a `.split()` result treated as text): "`.split()` handed back a list, so `words` holds a list, not text. Use the method on the text, or on one item: `words[0].upper()`." (5) "AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'append'" (8A-01): "Text has no `.append`. Glue it on with `+`: `initials = initials + name[0]`." (6) "TypeError: string indices must be integers" (8A-01 `sign[0, 9]`): reuse the comma-in-brackets help but say 'place' for text: "Inside `[ ]`, a slice takes a colon: `sign[0:9]`. A comma asks for two places at once." (7) "TypeError: object of type 'int' has no len()" (9X): "`len()` counts the letters in text or the items in a list. `blocks` holds a number, so there is nothing to count." (8) "TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, int found" (8P1 task 5): "`.join()` glues text only, and this list holds numbers. Join the text marks, or make each one text with `str()`." (9) "SyntaxError: f-string: expecting '}'" (8B-07, the QC f-string step): "Each `{` in an f-string needs its `}`." (10) `'str' object has no attribute 'Upper'` (and other capitalised method names): "Method names are all small letters: `.upper()`."
